messages:
Sarah: Ran an nsys sweep across a repro for the KV-cache prefetch path. Seeing repeated H2D gaps that line up with kvcache prefetch work + peerCopy bursts. timeline looks like: large host-to-device quiesce -> tiny kernel bursts -> long idle -> repeat.

Ben: can you paste the timeline snippet? wondering if it's pinned/pageable behaviour or kernel scheduling.

Sarah: pasted excerpt (trimmed):
```
[nsys timeline]
Time(ms) 0-1200
Host memcpy H2D (pageable) 0-40
kernel: kvcache_prefetch 45-60
idle 60-300
peerCopy H2D p2p 300-330
kernel: kv_insert 335-340
idle 340-900
```
Note: peaks coincide with peerCopy calls triggered by cross-GPU KV hotset sync.

Omar: pageable H2D will block the CPU thread until transfer finishes, so if we're doing lots of small memcpy()s that could serialize. Do we use cudaMemcpyAsync + pinned pools anywhere here?

Sarah: repro was using our default allocator (fallback pageable for small buffers). I reran with --use-pinned-kvpool and the H2D spans collapsed into fewer, larger transfers and the idle gaps mostly disappeared. latency improved ~18% for tail in this run.

Leah: nice. Did you also try consolidating prefetch requests into one batched memcpy? Batching can reduce PCIe bus contention and kernel launch jitter.

Sarah: yes, I added batching at the request router (coalesced prefetch windows). Results: further smoothing of timeline, plus reduced PCIe Tx bursts. But there's a catch — with NVLink peerCopy we still see occasional 8-12ms stalls that correlate to page-fault handling when a page is not pinned on the source.

Ben: that smells like pageable -> pinned promotion during peerCopy, causing kernel context switches while the driver pins pages. Did you capture perf events on the host?

Sarah: perf top didn't show obvious syscalls, but I captured a brief perfetto trace with mm/page fault markers. The pattern: pagefault -> driver pins page -> vm_op -> GPU memcpy resumes. Occurs when our prefetch window touches newly-allocated KV pages (small allocations).

Omar: two actionable hypotheses: 1) keep a hot pinned slab for kvcache pages to avoid pinning on demand, 2) coalesce allocations so we pin larger contiguous ranges ahead of transfers. Which is easier to try quickly?

Leah: hot pinned slab is quick (allocate large pinned pool at startup). Also try madvise(MADV_NOHUGEPAGE) avoid hugepage interactions? Not sure relevant but worth checking.

Sarah: I'll prototype pinned-slab + aggregation tomorrow. Also noticed kernel selection: when we switch to quantized kernel path (int8 path) the compute kernels are slightly faster but the transfer-to-compute ratio shifts and makes the prefetch gaps more visible. So kernel selection interacts with batching heuristics.

Ben: interesting — optimization removes compute bottleneck exposing IO. We should add a microbenchmark that sweeps kernel variants while varying prefetch concurrency and pinned vs pageable. Put the test under eng-runtime/perf-tests.

perf-bot: automated run completed: 1839457000 - nsys H2D-pinned-vs-pageable quick-sweep. Summary: pinned pool reduces number of H2D ops by ~60% and lowers 95th P99 by ~22%. Full logs: /perf/artifacts/1839457000.nsys

Omar: can someone run nvidia-smi topo -m and share topology? NVLink lanes may be asymmetric and can explain why some peerCopy combos are worse.

Sarah: posted topo output in thread gist: nvlink between GPU0-GPU1 is present, GPU1-GPU2 falls back to pcie. The bad bursts were between GPUs that needed a two-hop route.

Leah: that explains it. two-hop peer copies + pageable pages = double pin overhead. Action items: (1) Sarah -> prototype pinned slab + allocation coalescing (2) Ben -> add microbench that sweeps kernel variants + prefetch concurrency (3) Omar -> run full nsys capture with pinned slab and two-hop peer copies to measure residual stalls.

Sarah: ack. I'll attach nsys profiles and a short perf summary when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
